# AndroiOS

> AndroiOS is an open-source, sideloaded iOS/iPadOS app that runs Android (LineageOS 23.2 / Android 16) as an AArch64 virtual machine using QEMU's JIT, with Android's OpenGL ES graphics translated to Metal on the Apple GPU. Status: early alpha (v0.2.1-alpha), tested on a real iPhone (iPhone 16 Pro).

## What it does
- Boots the prebuilt LineageOS 23.2 virtio_arm64only VM (UEFI → GRUB → Android) inside the app process on iPhone and iPad.
- Renders Android's graphics on the Apple GPU (Metal) and shows them in a SwiftUI app.
- Forwards touch (USB tablet device), keyboard, audio (AC97 → AVAudioEngine) and networking (user-mode NAT via libslirp).

## How it works
- CPU: emulation, not virtualization. iOS gives apps no hypervisor, so QEMU's TCG JIT translates every guest instruction. JIT must be enabled with StikDebug (debugger-attached JIT); executable memory uses split RW/RX mappings to satisfy iOS W^X.
- GPU path: Android GLES → Mesa virgl → virtio-gpu → QEMU → virglrenderer → libepoxy → ANGLE (GLES on Metal) → Apple GPU → IOSurface → MTKView.
- The GPU components are the ones UTM ships on iOS: utmapp/virglrenderer, utmapp/libepoxy, and ANGLE from utmapp/WebKit, at UTM's pinned commits.
- QEMU 9.2.4 is built as an in-process framework (iOS forbids fork/exec), with patches for iOS JIT, an IOSurface display backend, an audio backend, and input injection.

## Requirements
- iPhone or iPad with an A13 chip or newer; 8 GB RAM devices or M-series iPads recommended (Android 16 is tight on 4 GB devices).
- Sideloading (AltStore, SideStore, TrollStore, or Xcode).
- Memory entitlements: com.apple.developer.kernel.increased-memory-limit and com.apple.developer.kernel.extended-virtual-addressing (via GetMoreRAM, TrollStore, or a paid developer profile).
- JIT via StikDebug with the universal.js script (required on iOS 26+ devices with TXM, A15 and newer).

## Performance (measured in a Mac harness running the iOS engine code, Apple A18 Pro GPU)
- LineageOS boot animation: 40–50 FPS. Boot to setup wizard: ~3–5 minutes.
- glmark2 GPU benchmark: score 103 (67–131 FPS per scene).
- Android UI is CPU-bound under emulation and does not reach 60 FPS.

## Status and known issues
- Tested on a real iPhone (iPhone 16 Pro, A18 Pro, iOS 26+): JIT works through StikDebug's universal.js script, and LineageOS 23.2 boots on the device.
- Verified in the Mac harness running the same engine code: boot, GPU rendering with readable text, touch, audio.
- v0.2.1-alpha addresses freezes (VM paused on iOS memory warnings) and crashes (iOS memory limit) on phones without the increased-memory-limit entitlement: memory warnings now shrink the guest through virtio-balloon, and guest RAM defaults to what iOS allows the app.
- Earlier fixes: v0.2.0-alpha fixed a crash at launch with JIT on iOS 26+ (AndroiOS uses the universal.js protocol: brk #0xf00d, x16=1 to prepare a region, x16=0 to detach) and SideStore's "The file can't be opened" (the 10 MB IPA downloads LineageOS in its setup wizard).

## Relationship to UTM
UTM is a mature, general-purpose VM app for iOS/macOS. AndroiOS is an Android-only app that reuses UTM's GPU components and bundles LineageOS for one-tap setup. UTM is the more mature option.

## Licensing
AndroiOS's own code is MIT-licensed. Its QEMU patches are GPL-2.0-or-later; virglrenderer and libepoxy are MIT, ANGLE is BSD-3-Clause, and LineageOS is under its own licenses.
